Topic T1 · First Impression

Where You'd Find It
The sample box catalog card — Item G1 lives in column G, row 1: /ACCURAPI2734, 7/32 X 5/8 X 3/32 flat washer rubber.
The physical box: each card on the lid lines up with a compartment below it. G1 is the compartment in the front row, on the right.

What You'd Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item G1 is a small, flat black washer. There is no head, no thread and no plating: just a disc with a round hole, made of rubber.

Center Hole (ID) — the round opening in the middle. Its diameter is the inner diameter, always a little larger than the screw or bolt that passes through it.

Flat Disc (OD) — a flat, ring-shaped disc, like a flattened doughnut. Its overall width is the outer diameter.

Black Rubber — solid black SBR rubber, the material that lets the washer seal a gap and conform to the surface it sits on.

Thin Profile — a low, flat edge, only 3/32 in thick, so it sits flush between the surfaces it separates.

Tap an orange dot to see what that feature is.

Topic T4 · Flat Washers

What Is a Flat Washer?

A flat washer is generally a disc shaped like a flattened doughnut, typically used with threaded fasteners.

How a Flat Washer Is Installed

  1. Select the size. Pick the flat washer that corresponds to the fastener.
  2. Place it. The washer goes on the bearing surface around the hole, or the fastener is placed on top of the washer, before the fastener is driven in.
  3. Tighten. The fastener is tightened to complete the installation.
Flat washers come in many sizes and materials, and are typically used with threaded fasteners (click to enlarge).
Why Use a Flat Washer?
Red arrows show the bearing surface pressure. With a flat washer it is spread out (click to enlarge).

Without a Flat Washer

The pressure from the fastener is concentrated on a small area, so the bearing surface can sink under the load and the joint can loosen.

With a Flat Washer

The bearing surface pressure is dispersed, which reduces the risk of the surface sinking and the resulting looseness.

Distribute the Load

Also known as plain washers, flat washers distribute the fastener's load while reducing heat and friction during the tightening process.

Work as Spacers

Flat washers can also be used as spacers, which is common in industrial and domestic applications.

Our washer is also made of a specific material. See why in .

Topic T5 · Rubber & SBR

Rubber Washers and SBR

The word “RUBBER” in the description changes what this washer is for: it is built to seal as well as to spread a load.

Purpose

A rubber washer's main purpose is to prevent leakage or seepage of fluids or gases between the surfaces it sits between. It acts as a barrier that seals off openings or gaps and stops the flow of air, water or other fluids.

Conforms to Surfaces

Rubber is preferred over other materials for its ability to conform to surfaces, and for its resistance to chemicals and extreme temperatures.

Highly Flexible

It can be easily manipulated into the desired shape or size.

Why Black?

Black is a very common attribute for rubber parts.

What “SBR” Means

SBR stands for styrene butadiene rubber: a general-purpose synthetic rubber and a cost-effective alternative to natural rubber (NR).

SBR vs. Natural Rubber

SBR shares most of the same characteristics as natural rubber, but it is manufactured from petroleum byproducts rather than latex.

Topic T6 · Hardness

Durometer: How Hard Is 70-75?

Hardness is the last piece of the extended description, and it matters for rubber more than for almost any other material.

What “Duro” Means

Short for durometer, the gauge used to measure the hardness of rubber.

The Shore Scale

The Shore scale is the one most commonly used for rubbers. It runs from 0 to 100: lower values are softer, higher values are harder.

This Washer: Duro 70-75

Our washer's hardness has a value of 70 to 75, so it is considered a medium hard part.

The Shore hardness chart, from extra soft to extra hard, with everyday objects as reference points. A 70-75 reading lands in the medium hard range (click to enlarge).

Topic T7 · Item Master in P21

What P21 Tells You

In P21, go to Item Maintenance and enter the part number. Notes, suppliers and customer classes all live on the same item record.

Item Notes

What Item Notes Are

Notes that highlight important information everyone working on the part should be aware of. They are the first thing you see in item maintenance.

Country of Origin

It affects the duty rate and tariffs depending on where parts are sent, which in turn affects our selling price and/or margin. Essential for account managers, buyers and planners.

Item Notes tab: COO is USA. This part is currently made in the USA.
Supplier List
Supplier List: Accurate Products, Inc. is indeed one of the suppliers, alongside another distributor, Spae-Naur Inc. Buying catalog parts from several distributors, depending on price and available stock, is common.
Customer Classes in Master Inquiry
Item Master Inquiry, company 100: Class 4 (BRP) and Class 5 (PPAP Level 4).

Class 5 · PPAP Level 4

These parts can normally be bought from several suppliers and do not require the customer's approval to introduce new vendors.

Class 4 · BRP

BRP is a special case among our customers: using a new supplier requires the approval of the SBS engineering team.

How a Catalog Washer Is Inspected

No Print: That's Normal

Very common for a catalog part. For a washer you only need the material, the potential finish, ID, OD and thickness — all of which are already in the part description.

The Inspection Template

Opening it shows that all of those criteria are inspected.

The Inspection Report
The inspection template, opened from P21 (click to enlarge).

When No Tolerance Is Given

When the customer or the manufacturer provides no tolerance, the quality team treats the dimensions as REF (for reference). As long as the inspected samples have dimensions close to the requirements, that is enough to consider the parts conforming.

Topic T9 · The QIP Twin

Same Part, Different Number

Back on the SBS website, a second item appeared with /QIP added to the end of the part number. Same description, different purpose.

/ACCURAPI2734

The current part. Bought from American distributors: Accurate Products and Spae-Naur.

/ACCURAPI2734/QIP

The same part, being developed with other suppliers. In P21, “QIP Part” is added to the extended description. Only one supplier is listed.

What QIP Stands For

QIP stands for quality and process. SBS uses it to tell a current part apart from the same part being developed with other suppliers for quality or cost-saving reasons. A similar but different part number avoids mixing current parts with parts that are not approved yet.

On the Website
Searching /ACCURAPI2734 on the SBS site returns two items: the part itself and the same number with /QIP added. The QIP item has no photo yet and is not in stock.
The QIP Supplier
The QIP item's supplier list shows only one supplier, different from the American distributors: Qingdao Dejay Automotive Component Co., Ltd.
Click the supplier ID to open Vendor Supplier Management and see the vendor's mail address. As the name suggests, this is a Chinese supplier.

Where to Look Next

To find out what is going on with a QIP part, consult the POD system — that is the subject of a different training.

Reference

Glossary

Every code, acronym, and term used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term's “jump” button to see it in context.

BRP

Bombardier Recreational Products — one of SBS's customers. A part with a BRP class needs SBS engineering approval before a new supplier is used.

Catalog Part

A part bought from a supplier's catalog rather than built to an SBS print. Catalog parts are commonly bought from several distributors, and often come with an inspection template instead of a print.

COO (Country of Origin)

Where the part is made. It affects duty rates and tariffs, and therefore selling price and margin. Recorded in the item notes in P21.

Durometer (Duro)

The gauge used to measure the hardness of rubber, and the “DURO” value in the description. This washer is 70-75, medium hard.

Flat Washer

A disc shaped like a flattened doughnut, used with threaded fasteners to distribute load, reduce heat and friction, and sometimes act as a spacer. Also called a plain washer.

ID / OD

Inner diameter and outer diameter of a washer. The ID is always larger than the mating screw or bolt so that nothing interferes on assembly.

P21

The SBS ERP system. Item Maintenance and Item Master Inquiry hold the notes, suppliers, classes and documents for every item.

PPAP Level 4

Production Part Approval Process, level 4. Parts with this class can normally be bought from several suppliers without the customer's approval for new vendors.

QIP

Quality and process. A suffix used to separate a current part from the same part being developed with other suppliers for quality or cost-saving reasons.

REF (Reference)

When no tolerance is provided by the customer or the manufacturer, the quality team treats the dimensions as reference values. Samples with close dimensions are considered conforming.

SBR

Styrene butadiene rubber. A general-purpose synthetic rubber, made from petroleum byproducts rather than latex, and a cost-effective alternative to natural rubber (NR).

Shore Scale

The scale most commonly used to measure rubber hardness. It runs from 0 to 100; lower is softer, higher is harder.
